drift_observation.note: dev did not drift in these runs: its 3 cold runs gave byte-identical text on all 6 prompts, and the probe builds gave bit-identical per-token logits and final-hidden-row hashes (2 dev, 2 pr0 runs x 600 tokens). The run lacked every documented trigger of the race: (1) no long first request (6 one-sentence prompts, TTFT 3.9-7.5 s; on a development tree with the same copies, runs differed from the first decode step after a long first request, pr0 commit b2c8ca61); (2) the default mirror budget (DSV4_CUDA_EXPERT_MIRRORS unset; a smaller budget made the drift show within a few tokens and flip a token in 2 of 3 runs, b2c8ca61); (3) no double bank (COLI_CUDA_MOE_DOUBLE unset; with it, 10-14 PR #1 arm C diverged in 2 of 3 cold runs before the fix); (4) refills not forced onto the pageable path (DSV4_CUDA_PIN_HOST unset, so refill sources were page-locked up to the 20 GiB cap, and dev queues page-locked refills on the compute stream; the PR #0 harness used DSV4_CUDA_PIN_HOST=0; whether any refill here went past the cap was not logged). The upload race pr0 fixes is timing-dependent, so this is no evidence that dev is race-free, and this manifest makes no claim that pr0 fixes a drift observed here. Probe builds ran at parity with the plain builds on the same two prompts (decode_0, decode_1; mean of the two per sample): D 2.6975/2.73/2.732, Z 2.72/2.736/2.741, Dp 2.735/2.735, Zp 2.746/2.7435 tok/s; probe/plain 1.0018x (dev) and 1.0032x (pr0) on medians, within 0.6% on means, so the logging did not slow decode. phase2 mean_tok_s is over these 2 prompts and phase-1 tok_s over all 6, so the two are not comparable directly. See stats.json phase2.

speed_comparison.note: pr0 median 2.8915 vs dev 2.8825 tok/s: +0.31%, below the 1% no-change threshold, so the outcome is no-change. Every pr0 sample is faster than every dev sample, but with n=3 per arm Welch's t = 2.52 (df 3.2), two-sided p = 0.08: not significant. Read: pr0 does not slow decode here; this is no evidence of a speed-up either.

conclusion: No drift was reproduced: dev 7b55a9b3 and pr0 a2c8ba7a gave byte-identical greedy text across 3 cold runs each and against each other on all 6 prompts, and the probe builds gave bit-identical per-token logit and final-hidden hashes (2 dev, 2 pr0 runs x 600 tokens). The run lacked every documented trigger of the race: (1) no long first request (6 one-sentence prompts, TTFT 3.9-7.5 s; on a development tree with the same copies, runs differed from the first decode step after a long first request, pr0 commit b2c8ca61); (2) the default mirror budget (DSV4_CUDA_EXPERT_MIRRORS unset; a smaller budget made the drift show within a few tokens and flip a token in 2 of 3 runs, b2c8ca61); (3) no double bank (COLI_CUDA_MOE_DOUBLE unset; with it, 10-14 PR #1 arm C diverged in 2 of 3 cold runs before the fix); (4) refills not forced onto the pageable path (DSV4_CUDA_PIN_HOST unset, so refill sources were page-locked up to the 20 GiB cap, and dev queues page-locked refills on the compute stream; the PR #0 harness used DSV4_CUDA_PIN_HOST=0; whether any refill here went past the cap was not logged). So this neither shows dev race-free nor demonstrates the fix end to end; the race itself is shown by PR #0's single-GPU harness (a refill in place under a queued fused MoE read the refilled expert in 50 of 50 and 300 of 300 trials on the unfixed backend, in none with the fix; b2c8ca61) and by the 10-14 double-bank divergence before the fix. Speed: pr0 median 2.8915 vs dev 2.8825 tok/s: +0.31%, below the 1% no-change threshold, so the outcome is no-change. Every pr0 sample is faster than every dev sample, but with n=3 per arm Welch's t = 2.52 (df 3.2), two-sided p = 0.08: not significant. Read: pr0 does not slow decode here; this is no evidence of a speed-up either.
